prompt: Two scenarios have the same four arrivals and fixed signal phases, yet finish with different queues. What accounts for the difference?

options.text: The model has selected a better controller for one scenario.
options.feedback: Both scenarios use the same phase sequence. Look at when each vehicle arrives relative to a green slot.

options.text: The timing of arrivals changes which vehicles can depart within the eight slots.
options.feedback: The rule serves the active green group after arrivals join its queue. An arrival that misses that group’s green can still be waiting at the end.

options.text: The smaller final queue establishes a shorter average wait in city traffic.
options.feedback: The trace counts vehicles remaining at one horizon. It contains neither a mean waiting-time measure nor observed city traffic.

prompt: What should be saved so a colleague can use this experiment in the next investigation?

options.text: The model revision, scenario edit, observation horizon, queue result and next question.
options.feedback: These details connect the observation to the exact assumptions and inputs that produced it and make the follow-up reproducible.

options.text: Only the smallest queue shown by the experiment.
options.feedback: A count on its own omits the arrival pattern, model revision and time at which it was taken.

options.text: An instruction to use the simulated schedule for the real intersection.
options.feedback: A source-linked observation supports the next investigation. Choosing an operational schedule requires evidence about the real system.
